business_scope.primary_industry_name: Middle-Market Cross-Border Cross-Industry M&A Advisory Boutique

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic continental tradition); statutory commercial law codified in the Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971); special simplified joint-stock company regime in Ley 1258 de 2008
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (CTPA, in force 2012)
Colombia-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)
Colombia-Spain Double Taxation Agreement (in force per Ley 1287 de 2009)
Colombia-Mexico Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: UBO and AML/CFT obligations derive primarily from Ley 526 de 1999 (creation of the UIAF), Ley 1121 de 2006, Ley 1621 de 2013, Decreto 1674 de 2016 (as amended by Decreto 830 de 2021), Resolución UIAF No. 103 de 2021 (uniform beneficial-owner declaration and reporting), Circular Externa No. 100-000005 de 2021 of the Superintendencia de Sociedades (SARLAFT for the real sector), and the Circular Básica Jurídica of the Superintendencia Financiera; cross-border authentication of foreign corporate and personal documents is governed by Ley 1556 de 2012 on the Hague Apostille Convention and by Resolution 00393 of 2021 of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the foreign passport of each non-resident shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record / police clearance certificate of each non-resident director or UBO who has been resident abroad during the three years preceding the incorporation filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal records authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence and good standing of each foreign corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registrar of companies of the foreign state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: General or special Power of Attorney granted by each foreign shareholder in favor of the local incorporator or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation of each apostilled foreign document (by an officially certified translator)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator (traductor oficial) recognized in Colombia

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado de Antecedentes Judiciales (Colombian judicial background certificate) for each resident director or legal representative

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 4, 5, 17 and 22; Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), Title XI; Law 962 of 2005
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social via the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES); supervised by Superintendencia de Sociedades
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation deed) with optional notarial protocolization, filed for registration in the RUES
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for S.A.S. under Law 1258 of 2008; founders fix subscribed capital freely but must pay it within two years (Art. 5). Escrow is not mandatory; cash contributions are evidenced by bank records, in-kind contributions require a sworn appraiser certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: the capital subscription and payment schedule in the incorporation instrument are ratified, and shares are allotted to the founding subscribers as recorded. RESOLVED SECOND: the registered office at [address], Bogotá D.C., is adopted as the statutory domicile. RESOLVED THIRD: [Name] is appointed President and legal representative, and [Name] is appointed Secretary; each has full power to execute filings, sign contracts, open bank accounts, and appoint attorneys. RESOLVED FOURTH: the President is designated AML/CFT compliance officer and is directed to implement the firm's KYC risk-control program before commencing M&A advisory services; the corporate governance manual is adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio – RUES online homonymy search (Registro de Homonimia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name-validation application to the chamber of the intended domicile. The certificate (certificado de homonimia) reserves the proposed legal name for 30 days and certifies that no confusingly similar entity is registered. After receipt, keep the certificate to attach to the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and spelling variants
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is denied or flagged as similar, file a second online request with 2–3 alternative names and pay the reseach fee; the certificate is re-issued within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público (any Colombian notary) or authorized digital-signature provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the private incorporation deed covering the corporate name, domicile, duration, purpose (ISIC 7020 / M&A advisory), share capital, classes of shares, representation rules, and first officers. All founders sign the deed before a notary to authenticate signatures and date. The notary returns a certified copy (copia auténtica) for subsequent registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all founding shareholders
Proof of payment of subscribed shares (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies missing parties or insufficient documentation, schedule a second signing session or use a power-of-attorney; re-execute and re-certify the deed before paying the registration fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration in the Cámara de Comercio/RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) via RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified incorporation deed together with the single registration form (Formulario de Registro Único Empresarial) and pay the registration fee plus the municipal registration tax (impuesto de registro). The chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, confirming the company is fully incorporated and the legal representative is registered.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the legal representative
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chamber issues a deficiency notice, cure the discrepancy within 20 business days by uploading the missing documents; if registration is refused, appeal before the chamber's legal department and subsequently to Superintendencia de Sociedades.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax identification and e-invoicing registration with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (virtual portal Muisca / Pre-RUT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online pre-registration (Pre-RUT) using the certificate of existence and legal representation, select the main economic activity 7020 (business consulting) with ISIC v4 code 7020 and NAICS 523150 as secondary, and obtain the definitive NIT plus electronic signature (firma electrónica). Activate the e-invoicing obligation (factura electrónica) and verify entry in the ESFA for transfer-pricing compliance.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Identity document of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the pre-RUT, correct the data in the virtual office and resubmit; for persistent errors, raise a service ticket in Muisca or visit the local DIAN attention point with a written justification and supporting documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos (e.g., Bomberos de Bogotá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the fire-safety form (Certificado de Bomberos) for the leased office premises, indicating the load capacity, evacuation plan, and fire-extinguishing equipment. For low-risk professional offices, a declared form with documentary inspection is accepted; after verification, the certificate is issued and must be renewed annually.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Uso del Suelo (land use certificate)
Lease agreement or proof of property possession
Fire extinguisher and detection equipment list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspection declares non-compliance, implement the required corrective measures, attach photographic evidence, and request a new inspection; any fine may be appealed before the municipal mayor's office within the legal term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating license and civil defense clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Local / Secretaría Distrital de Planeación; Defensa Civil Colombiana
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prior operating communication (comunicación de inicio de actividades) under Decreto 1879 de 2008, together with the Certificado de Uso del Suelo and the fire-safety certificate. For office-only professional services, the municipal operating license (Licencia de Funcionamiento) is issued automatically for compatible uses. Concurrently enroll in the municipal industria y comercio (ICA) tax register. Civil defense clearance verifies maximum occupancy and evacuation routes.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the zoning determination rejects the use, select an address in a compatible office-commercial zone or file an engineering and usage concept with the local planning authority; appeal the adverse zoning decision before the Secretaría Distrital de Planeación within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Planeación / Alcaldía Local via the municipal one-stop window (Ventanilla Única de Registro); Superintendencia de Sociedades as corporate oversight body
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Funcionamiento de Establecimiento Comercial (Decreto 1879 de 2008) combined with the Certificado de Uso del Suelo; no sectoral financial license is required for advisory-only M&A mandates

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA); local jurisdiction exercised by Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) for physical retrofitting works
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 — Exempt: office-only professional services are exempt from an environmental license under Law 99 of 1993 and Decreto 1076 de 2015; a simple municipal environmental registration covers signage and non-hazardous waste generation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater not connected to a sewer must meet Resolución 0631 de 2015 (DBO5 ≤ 40 mg/L, SST ≤ 40 mg/L); segregated solid waste per Resolución 2184 de 2019; any emergency generator must comply with Resolución 2254 de 2017 (PM2.5 24h = 50 µg/m³)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification by the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos (annual renewal), structural load verification of leased premises per the NSR-10 building code, SG-SST occupational health implementation under Decreto 1072 de 2015 before personnel deployment, and Defensa Civil inspection for office capacity and evacuation routes

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); online portal: MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) at www.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Colombian SAS must complete (i) incorporation before the Cámara de Comercio, which electronically transmits the registral data and obtains automatic issuance of the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), and (ii) formal registration in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) via DIAN's MUISCA portal or an authorized service center. Required items: certified articles of incorporation (certificado de existencia y representación legal), legal representative identification (valid Colombian cédula or foreign passport with local immigration status), local registered office address, description of economic activity (ISIC 7020 accepted), and evidence of non-resident shareholder status for foreign owners. RUT must be kept current and may be completed online for standard cases; no minimum capital is required for the SAS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a check-the-box or US-style disregarded entity election. The SAS may irrevocably elect taxation under the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) if annual gross income does not exceed 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 174,296,500 for tax year 2025) and the activity qualifies; it may also elect the special VAT regime provisions applicable to exported services. No hybrid mismatch elections are available; BEPS Action 2 outcomes are addressed through domestic CFC and permanent establishment rules under Laws 1943/2018 and 2010/2019, which impose mandatory disclosure on aggressive tax structures rather than elective treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto al Valor Agregado) – national value added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for companies: every SAS engaged in taxable transactions in Colombia must obtain NIT/RUT and register as a VAT-responsible taxpayer ab initio, irrespective of volume. The only proportional threshold is the SIMPLE regime opt-in limit of 3,500 UVT for small taxpayers, not a VAT registration exemption; VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable operation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory, statute-driven electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta). All invoices must be transmitted in real time to DIAN for 'validación previa' (prior validation) before delivery to the client; DIAN assigns a CUDE (Código Único de Documento Electrónico) and a machine-readable digital stamp (QR code). Taxpayers must use DIAN-authorised software providers or DIAN's free electronic invoicing application; API/SFTP integration is compulsory for taxpayers exceeding DIAN's volume thresholds. An invoice that fails DIAN validation is legally ineffective for cost deduction and input VAT credit purposes, and late or non-transmission triggers daily fines under Articles 615 and 652-13 of the Estatuto Tributario.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods physically dispatched from Colombian customs territory qualifies for 0% VAT (exclusion from the taxable base). Cross-border M&A advisory services (ISIC 7020) qualify as export of services excluded from IVA when: (i) the service is rendered to a non-resident beneficiary without domicile in Colombia, (ii) the service is effectively used or exploited outside Colombia, and (iii) the SAS maintains documentary evidence of both facts in accordance with Decree 1625 of 2016, Article 1.6.1.13.2 et seq. The SAS must retain VAT-responsible status and continue filing periodic returns even when all transactions are zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX) filed through DIAN/SICE customs system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit of goods from Colombian customs territory
Commercial invoice and foreign currency payment proof (SWIFT MT103 from the overseas client)
RUT and the relevant VAT return (F-300) demonstrating zero-rating treatment
Advisory services contract / engagement letter linking the service to the foreign beneficiary and to use/exploitation outside Colombia
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN subjects zero-rating claims to rigorous documentary and transactional audit. Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating triggers: retroactive VAT assessment on the full invoice amount, monthly default interest (currently 1.5% per month), inaccuracy penalty (sanción por inexactitud) of up to 200% of the tax involved under Articles 647 of the Estatuto Tributario as amended by Law 2277 of 2022, customs fines, and potential seizure of goods for false export declarations. Where intent is proven, criminal prosecution under Articles 434B and 435 of the Código Penal and anti-smuggling Law 1762 of 2015 may result in imprisonment, disqualification of the legal representative, cancellation of export benefits, and clawback of any VAT refunds previously received, with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (the Central Bank of Colombia), acting jointly with the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Financial Superintendence of Colombia (Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia) as the competent authority under the Colombian Foreign Exchange Regime (Régimen de Cambios Internacionales), principally contained in Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1735 of 1993, and Banco de la República Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso is freely convertible for current-account and capital-account operations, but every cross-border flow must be 'canalizada' through authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries registered with Banco de la República. M&A advisory fees and success fees arising from cross-border services are treated as services-export proceeds and must be channeled back into Colombia through the foreign exchange market. Profit remittances are permissible after corporate income tax has been satisfied, but require proof of distributable earnings, shareholder approval, filing of the applicable foreign-exchange declaration, and compliance with dividend withholding tax rules. Capital contributions by non-resident shareholders are classified as foreign direct investment and require registration with Banco de la República; such registration is a precondition for subsequent dividend remittance and exit transactions. No blanket prohibition on profit repatriation exists, but delays or procedural omissions in FX declarations can trigger sanctions and loss of access to the official exchange market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds, including M&A advisory fees from foreign clients, must be repatriated through an authorized Colombian foreign-exchange intermediary within the statutory six-month term prescribed under the Colombian exchange regime measured from the invoice or completion milestone for services. There is no mandatory fixed-percentage conversion into Colombian pesos; the exporter may retain the funds in a foreign-currency-denominated bank account located in Colombia provided the proceeds have been properly channeled and the corresponding electronic 'Declaración de Cambio' has been submitted through the receiving bank. Failures to channel, late repatriation, or monetization outside the authorized foreign-exchange market constitute exchange-control violations subject to fines and administrative penalties. The Colombian banking intermediary is required to verify the export nature of the proceeds and assign the correct purpose code before accepting the remittance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in COP and USD; Capital Escrow Account for transaction proceeds
Operational Account; Foreign Currency Deposit Account (USD)
Operational Account; Escrow sub-account for M&A success fees
Operational Account; Cross-Border Payment Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as the primary treasury rail. A Colombian S.A.S. may legally open and use accounts with offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex, or Dukascopy, but such entities are not authorized Colombian foreign-exchange intermediaries and cannot process exports, capital injections, or regulated FX declarations. Offshore EMIs may serve only as auxiliary cards or disbursement channels for incidental expenses, provided all underlying Colombian-source operations are documented and mirrored through a local regulated bank. Heavy reliance on an EMI for inbound client fees or outbound success-fee payments will be treated as an AML red flag by Colombian banking partners and may constitute a breach of the mandatory channeling regime under Decree 1735 of 1993.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no absolute statutory mandate requiring every director to appear physically in a Colombian bank branch. Under Financial Superintendence regulations, banks may use remote digital identity verification and video interviews for corporate account opening, but the final risk decision belongs to each bank's compliance committee. For a Medium-Risk Enhanced M&A advisory boutique, the legal representative and at least one final beneficial owner must complete a notarized identity verification, produce the Chamber of Commerce certificate of existence and legal representation ('Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal'), and undergo a heightened due-diligence interview. In practice, tier-1 banks will require physical presence or notarized video presence of the legal representative to execute the account agreement; secondary directors may authenticate remotely if the legal representative authenticates before a notary. The KYC interview may be conducted in Spanish; all corporate documents must be current, apostilled if foreign, and accompanied by registered translations where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership of the S.A.S. and ambiguous control structure of the M&A advisory boutique.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chamber of Commerce certificate of existence and legal representation; updated registrations with the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB); notarized identification and specimen signatures of all directors and shareholders; corporate organizational chart; certified constitutional documents (estatutos sociales) of the S.A.S.; board resolution appointing signatories and approving account opening; sworn statement of the final beneficial owners explaining the source of funds for the activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Success fees and advisory proceeds originating from multiple non-resident third parties, including foreign sellers, buyers, and escrow agents not identified at the outset.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete M&A transaction folders; signed engagement letters and fee letters; buy-side and sell-side agreements; closing statements; escrow agreements and instruction letters; detailed invoices with milestone calculations; transaction charts showing the commercial rationale; signed declarations from foreign counterparties as to the legal origin and purpose of funds; SWIFT reference numbers tied to each counterparty; quarterly transaction monitoring reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to politically exposed persons (PEPs), high-risk jurisdictions, or foreign clients domiciled in tax havens without visible economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP screening results conducted at onboarding and periodically; certified passport copies and tax residency certificates of all foreign clients; source-of-wealth declarations; source-of-funds declarations supported by bank statements and transaction documents; corporate registry excerpts and proof of economic activity of the counterparty; commercial rationale memorandum; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire approved by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual frequency of cross-border FX transactions and large COP/USD sweeps ahead of closing dates, especially when combined with rapid return of funds to third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury and FX policy; projected cash-flow and transaction schedule; invoices and disbursement orders for each expected payment; underlying M&A engagement contracts; approved escrow mechanics and disbursement authorization forms; bank-purpose code certification; monthly accounting ledger and transaction trail; periodic filings with Banco de la República confirming channeling of all receipts and payments; compliance attestation signed by the external auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign share capital injections into the Colombian S.A.S. must be received as SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the shareholder's foreign bank account to the entity's USD or COP operating account maintained at a local commercial bank. The local bank must classify the remittance using the appropriate foreign-exchange purpose code for 'foreign direct investment in companies' and issue the corresponding electronic foreign-exchange declaration ('Declaración de Cambio') to Banco de la República. If the incoming amount constitutes a registered foreign investment, the S.A.S. must complete the foreign-investment registration with Banco de la República using the proper investment-registration form and maintain proof for future remittances. The instructing bank must include a clear payment narrative referencing the entity's NIT (tax identification number), the corporate purpose, the shareholder's name, and the capital subscription agreement. Inbound amounts below the minimum registration threshold may be received through the simplified channel of the local bank, but the forming documentation and board resolutions must still evidence that funds are equity, not debt, and not proceeds needing export-channeling treatment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for cross-border M&A advisory engagements, including commissions to sub-agents, external legal counsel, valuation firms, or the return of client monies, must be cleared through the entity's local regulated bank using SWIFT MT103 or equivalent correspondent banking rails. The payment must be classified under the correct foreign-exchange service code and accompanied by a signed commercial invoice, engagement contract, or disbursement instruction demonstrating the purpose of the transaction. The bank will generate the corresponding foreign-exchange declaration for exit reporting. Withholding taxes and the bank debit tax (Gravamen a los Movimientos Financieros) must be settled at the time of payment when applicable. Commercial letters of credit are not a viable or appropriate clearing rail for M&A advisory fees; they should be used solely for goods transactions. For deterministic milestone payments, SWIFT MT103 provides real-time traceability, payment confirmation, and matching with the invoice reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts with authorized Colombian foreign-exchange intermediaries, limited to hedging of documented current-account exposures arising from cross-border M&A advisory receivables or payables.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in COP/USD referencing the official Colombian peso exchange rate, provided the underlying exposure is genuine, quantifiable, and evidenced by an outstanding service agreement or receivable.

Currency swaps executed with licensed Colombian banks or foreign banks through an authorized intermediary, used exclusively to hedge currency mismatches on cross-border transactions and not for speculative trading.

FX options and cross-currency interest-rate swaps where expressly authorized by Banco de la República and executed under a duly documented hedging relationship with an underlying trade or investment exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of mercantile registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) via the Registro Único Empresarial (RUE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for operations in the prior fiscal year ending 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal by the deadline triggers a fine of up to 15 SMMLV (approx. USD 21,400); continued non-renewal leads to administrative strike-off of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 9 April and 2 May of the following year, in accordance with the DIAN calendar based on the last two digits of the NIT.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subjects the company to fines of up to 1% of gross income or 5% of omitted tax, plus default interest; non-filing may trigger DIAN collection action and criminal charges in cases of deliberate evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the previous fiscal year (or the next business day if 31 March is non-working).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file, or submission of materially inaccurate data, may result in fines up to 15,000 UVT (approx. USD 180,000); mandatory corrections may also be imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio / Registro Único Empresarial (RUE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after approval by the shareholders' meeting, which must conveniently be held by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit the financial statements is an administrative infringement; the Chamber may impose discretionary fines, and continued omission blocks issuance of the annual commercial registration certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales - RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the first quarter of the year, no later than 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or incomplete information incurs penalties under Law 2155 of 2021 up to 1,800 UVT (approx. USD 21,000) and may also block renewal of the commercial registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A S.A.S. must appoint a statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) if at the preceding 31 December total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (COP approx. 7,100 million / USD approx. 1.7 million) or gross income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (COP approx. 4,300 million / USD approx. 1.05 million); also mandatory for entities under DIAN or Superintendencia de Sociedades supervision, listed securities, or if shareholders representing at least 20% of shares request it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS mandatory as adopted in Colombia (NIIF), with the preparer classified under Group 1 (full NIIF), Group 2 (NIIF para las PYMES) or Group 3 (NIIF para microempresas); M&A advisory boutiques are normally Group 2 unless public-interest or large-enterprise status invokes Group 1.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Colombia's final-beneficiary regime (Law 2155 of 2021 and DIAN Resolution 164 of 2023), the S.A.S. must update the RUBF annually during the first quarter (by 31 March). Any transfer of shares during the year changes the UBO data; the company must reflect that transfer in the shareholders' register and update DIAN's RUBF, with a change-based update due within one month of the transfer. The annual tax exogenous information filing also captures shareholder data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Minutes of Shareholders' Meetings (Libro de Actas de Asamblea)
Statutory Auditor's Book (when revisor fiscal is appointed)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – USD 1,200 annual registered agent / local compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 8,000 for a certified audit performed by a public accountant or audit firm; higher if full-scope consolidated audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory sectoral tax holiday or preferential rate applies to ISIC 7020 M&A advisory services. The effective corporate income tax burden for a standard SAS is the general 35% rate after ordinary deductions, with no industry-specific exemption or investment tax credit applicable to boutique M&A advisory activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 - Declaración de Renta y Complementarios, filed electronically through the DIAN portal MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Administrativo). The taxpayer also submits Form 1732/1733 (información tributaria) as applicable and the Transfer Pricing Annex when thresholds are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return is due according to the DIAN resolution-calendar, which for calendar-year taxpayers falls generally between mid-April and mid-May of the following fiscal year, based on the last two digits of the NIT. Taxpayers with a non-calendar fiscal year end use the deadlines set for such periods by DIAN, generally no later than three months after the close of the corresponding tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT, company name, economic activity code, fiscal year start/end, and reconciliation of prior-year tax status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Colombian NIT assigned to the SAS. For a SAS directly owned by non-residents, there is no alternative code; the entity is present due to incorporation in Colombia and must file as any domestic taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue derived from operations, including M&A advisory fees, successes, commissions, and retainer income from cross-border engagements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full amount of Colombian-source advisory income. Fees economically attributable to the Colombian SAS must be included regardless of the payment routing or the non-residence of the ultimate client.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 34 / Operating Costs and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses strictly related to the generation of the gross income: salaries, office rent, travel, professional fees, and essential subcontracting costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only costs supported by registered invoices or equivalent electronic documents and actually paid through Colombian or traceable foreign banking systems are deductible. Costs paid to related parties abroad are subject to transfer pricing arm's-length analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income that under the Colombian Tax Statute or an applicable double tax treaty is not treated as Colombian-source or is otherwise exempt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident asset owner entering into an onward M&A advisory arrangement cannot use this line unless a specific treaty article excludes the fee from Colombian-source income. Treaty protection must be evidenced by a valid residence certificate and filed with the return attachments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 90 / Liquid Income before Deductions and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the net taxable liquid income after allowable deductions and after taking into account the five-year fiscal loss carryforward, if any.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No loss carryforward is available to the extent the Colombian SAS is treated as dormant or as a transparent instrumentality for treaty purposes. All loss positions must pass the economic substance test.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an extemporaneity penalty equal to 5% of the tax liability for each month or fraction of a month, subject to a minimum penalty of 10 UVT (approx COP 470,650 in 2024) and a maximum penalty of 100% of the tax assessed. Late payment additionally generates moratory interest at DIAN's determined monthly interest rate. Understatement or inaccurate returns are subject to a 100% to 220% penalty on the higher tax owed, plus interest and potential criminal sanctions for wilful tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident beneficial owners of shares or quotas in a Colombian SAS. The rate is applied to distributions made from profit subject to corporate income tax. Dividends paid to shareholders residing in a non-cooperative / low-tax jurisdiction may be disqualified from the statutory treatment and subject to higher withholding and administrative re-characterization.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend withholding rate under an applicable double tax agreement (DTA), the non-resident beneficial owner must procure an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority, legalize it (Apostille/Convention or Colombian consular process if no Apostille applies), and submit a Spanish translation accompanied by a declaration of beneficial ownership to the Colombian paying entity before dividend distribution. The Colombian payer must retain the TRC to justify the reduced rate. If the payer applied the statutory 10% and a treaty permits a lower rate, the non-resident may file an administrative refund claim with DIAN within the applicable two-year prescription period, attaching the TRC and evidence of the withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on interest paid to foreign creditors is 15%; statutory withholding on royalties and technical-assistance fees paid abroad is generally 15%, with lower rates for certain software and know-how categories depending on the nature of the IP. Some Colombian double tax conventions reduce the source rate to 10% (or 5%-10% in specific qualifying circumstances) for interest and royalties, subject to the updated OECD-based limitations on benefits clause and TRC proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Colombian Transfer Pricing Documentation (Local File and, for groups, Master File) is triggered when, in a given fiscal year, related-party transactions exceed 10,000 UVT - COP 470,650,000 based on the 2024 UVT of COP 47,065 - or when the taxpayer's gross income and/or net wealth exceeds 125,000 UVT (approx COP 5,883,125,000). A separate declaration annex is due for taxpayers that engage in cross-border related-party transactions and satisfy the minima above.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia has no independent Economic Substance Regulation in the BVI/SAMOA sense, but the tax authorities apply the general anti-abuse provisions (Articles 669-679 E.T.), under which an SAS engaged in M&A advisory must have real premises, qualified personnel, actual management decisions, and a rational functional profile in Colombia. A letter-box entity, a nominee board, or a contract routed solely through a foreign holding structure without operational substance will be disregarded or re-characterized for Colombian income tax purposes, DTA benefit denial, and potential CFC / transfer pricing adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False or Manipulated Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting success-fee income arising from M&A transactions, issuing fictitious deductible invoices, or mischaracterizing taxable advisory income as non-taxable or exempt under an inappropriate treaty position. This includes holding a material office outside Colombia while directing the Colombian SAS's operations without registering taxable permanent establishment income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imposition of a 100% monumento inaccuracy penalty, increased to 220% where an abusive tax advantage is obtained, plus moratory interest. Criminal conviction for tax evasion can lead to imprisonment of four to eight years and a fine calculated on the understated tax, under Colombian anti-evasion legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who sign a knowingly false return become jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax debt, interest and penalties. The tax administration may seek preventive embargo of assets, interrogation, and judicial travel bans; a criminal conviction triggers debarment from corporate management and forfeiture of ill-gotten proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Split of Activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Colombian SAS purely as a pass-through vehicle to receive M&A advisory fees from Latin American clients and immediately distributing the profits to an offshore parent, while identifying the actual headquarters abroad and leaving the SAS with minimal employees, no office, and no management autonomy.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN can apply the abuse-of-legal-form doctrine, disregard the entity, re-characterize revenues as the parent's income and dividend payments as repatriation subject to the 10% withholding plus the 35% corporate tax at the entity level, or impose the 100%-220% penalty. Failure to file or filing a fraudulent TP report adds an additional 25% incomplete-documentation fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Colombian Tax Code provisions on liability of administrators, directors and shareholders who receive the diverted value can be held liable for the entity's unpaid tax and penalties. Director passports can be restricted, and civil lawsuits for restitution may attach because the corporate veil is pierced in cases of artificiality, contempt, or fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Cross-Border Bribery and Money Laundering through M&A Fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Acting as an unregulated M&A intermediary while accepting client funds via shell-company receivers, cash transactions, or offshore accounts without application of the mandatory know-your-client, beneficial-ownership, and suspicious-transaction controls under Colombian risk-management rules, especially when the factual context indicates proceeds from corruption or drug trafficking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to adopt and execute an adequate SAGRILAFT/AML system by an obligated entity or individual can generate administrative fines of several thousand UVT and cancellation of required licenses (including the statutory M&A activity license). If the activity is prosecuted as money laundering, the criminal sanction includes substantial imprisonment (generally more than eight years), asset confiscation and fines proportional to the laundered value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers of the boutique who designed or ignored the AML protocols face direct criminal liability, personal fines, sequestration of personal assets, bans on leaving the jurisdiction and, upon conviction, imprisonment. The corporate form does not shield the managers from the prohibited conduct, and each officer may be personally ordered to disgorge any fees obtained from the illegally structured transaction.
